issues.failure_explanation: A signed-distance function is not generally differentiable at points having multiple nearest boundary points, so the quotient defining \overline{n} and the asserted normal-coordinate representation are not available for every x in B. For example, the signed distance to a ball is nondifferentiable at its center. Moreover, the tanh phase field satisfies 0<\phi<1 at every point where r is finite, so the formulations use f and g throughout B rather than only in a tubular neighborhood where the nearest-point normal extension is well defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Construct the constant-normal extensions only in a tubular neighborhood with a single-valued nearest-point projection, and provide arbitrary suitable global extensions outside it (or use a compactly supported phase-field formulation that never evaluates them there).
issues.overall_effect: The stated extensions of f and g, and hence the right-hand sides of the diffuse-domain methods, are not defined as written for general domains and extended domains.
issues.title: The diffuse normal and normal extension are not globally defined
issues.why_classification: A genuine extension construction and corresponding localization are needed, but this can be contained near the definitions without replacing the paper's overall method or guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation:
The established diffusion energy contains |
abla(\phi u)|^2, whereas the asserted norm contains \phi|
abla u|^2. Expanding the former introduces cross terms involving u
abla\phi, so changing only the power of epsilon does not make it the DDM1 energy. A nontrivial estimate controlling the stated norm by the displayed SBM energy is missing.

failure_location.quote:
This is identical, up to epsilon scalling, to DDM1,
    so following the results (\cref{thm:ddm1_pd}),
    this method is coercive.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a valid estimate relating \|\nabla(\phi u)\| and the penalty term to the stated weighted gradient norm, with all required bounds on \phi and \nabla\phi, or weaken the theorem to coercivity in an energy norm directly defined by the displayed bilinear form.
issues.overall_effect: Coercivity of SBM in the stated norm is not proved, and the stabilized-advection SBM theorem inherits this gap because its proof treats SBM diffusion coercivity as established.
issues.title: The SBM coercivity proof compares different energies without a bound
issues.why_classification: The conclusion may admit a contained replacement estimate or a revised energy norm, but it does not follow by the cited argument and requires more than routine algebra.

issues.failure_explanation:
The actual mass-divergence contribution is \phi m-	frac12\phi^2
abla\cdot b, not \phi^2(m-	frac12
abla\cdot b). Their difference is \phi(1-\phi)m, whose sign is uncontrolled because the hypothesis permits m<0 when 
abla\cdot b is sufficiently negative. Thus the quoted nonnegative expression does not prove that the bilinear form's corresponding terms are nonnegative.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either impose an additional condition such as m\geq0 and redo the decomposition, or change the diffuse mass weighting to \phi^2m and re-establish the method and its numerical interpretation.
issues.overall_effect: Coercivity of the stated MixedO advection method is unsupported over the advertised elliptic-data regime.
issues.title: The MixedO advection coercivity argument mishandles the mass weighting
issues.why_classification: A local additional hypothesis or formulation change can repair the sign argument, but either narrows the stated parameter regime or changes the analyzed method.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the no-stabilization claim and state that the proved MixedZ formulation includes the displayed stabilization term, unless a new proof for the unstabilized formulation is provided.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed comparative advantage of MixedZ over methods requiring stabilization is unsupported, although the stabilized method's separate coercivity claim remains.
